adds.title: DPE-AM Working Group on Sexual Diversity, Gender Identity and Citizenship - 2021
adds.summary: On 28 June 2021 the Amazonas Public Defender's Office created the permanent Working Group on Sexual Diversity, Gender Identity and Citizenship to identify LGBTQIA+ human-rights violations in public security, train public-security agents for service to LGBTQIA+ people, and issue recommendations and extrajudicial measures, while LGBTQIA+ victims in Manaus can obtain assistance via Disk 129 Monday-Friday 8am-2pm through the Specialized Human Rights unit, in a context where Amazonas led North and Central-West states with 4.66 LGBTQIA+ persons murdered per million inhabitants in 2018.

adds.title: Nationwide criminalization of homophobia and transphobia - 2019
adds.summary: On 23 May 2019 a majority of Brazil's Supreme Federal Tribunal (6 of 11 justices) voted to criminalize transphobia under Brazil's 1989 racism law punishable by up to five years' imprisonment until Congress enacts specific LGBT-discrimination legislation, to take effect after all justices voted on 5 June 2019.

adds.title: Brazilian Public Security Forum / Brazilian Journal of Public Security data + Fernando Vilaca de Souza homicide 5 July 2025
adds.summary: In Amazonas during 2021-2022, crimes involving transsexual persons formed part of only 0.36% of total reported crimes in the capital and interior, police occurrence reports did not identify transfobia or gender, sexuality, race and intersectionality markers, trans victim data were few and badly structured with victims not infrequently inverted to accused through faulty BOs, and unprepared public agents and defective registration mechanisms left trans subjects invisibilized and without protection.
